steps.title: Write approved plan and progress tracker
steps.notes: Plan approved by user; tracking files created.

steps.title: Add Hono service, server-side @immich/sdk client, configuration, and authentication
steps.notes: Hono app on @hono/node-server with the server-side @immich/sdk 3.3.0-rc.0 client, environment/secret loading, Basic auth, JSON body limits, same-origin checks, security headers, and error-to-status mapping.

steps.title: Add date/album search and asset metadata access
steps.notes: Date/album search uses stable nested filters and cursor pagination from the supplied Immich OpenAPI spec.

steps.title: Add the selected fixed compression profiles and candidate size comparison
steps.notes: Fixed image profiles implemented; candidates must be strictly smaller. Live Photo video links are preserved and verified.

steps.title: Upload, copy and verify tags/albums, and optionally delete originals
steps.notes: Upload, tag/album assignment, checksum and metadata verification precede optional non-force deletion; default is keep.

steps.title: Add search, selection, comparison, progress, and apply UI flows
steps.notes: React SPA (Vite) with search, grid, profile selection, run controls, compare list, and batch review. Multi-profile runs optimize all selected images up front, three concurrently, then compare them one decision at a time with the smallest candidate highlighted; single-profile runs show a batch table with explicit apply. Stable React keys keep thumbnails attached across polls.

steps.title: Add a web Docker target and deployment instructions while preserving the proxy target
steps.notes: Shared-toolchain web Docker target and deployment documentation are written; Docker image was not built.

steps.title: Add monthly library endpoints: counts, month listing, trash, archive
steps.notes: Per-month capture counts come from one calendar-heatmap request; a month listing paginates internally, widens the UTC range and filters by local capture month, and is capped at 3000 assets. Trash uses a non-forced delete, archive sets visibility, and both validate UUID lists against a 500 id limit.

steps.title: Two-tab shell with Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui
steps.notes: The SPA moved to Tailwind v4 plus shadcn/ui (new-york/radix registry) with components.json, an @/* alias and generated components/ui. The compress tab was rewritten against the same components; the hand-written stylesheet was removed.

steps.title: Monthly cleanup flow: year grid, burst groups, per-asset actions
steps.notes: Year grid with counts; month view loads thumbnails only and splits same-minute bursts with a suggested keeper. Left click keeps, right click trashes, each burst group has an action bar, ungrouped assets get per-asset compress/trash/archive buttons, a profile selector drives compression, and every action confirms first. Compression reuses the existing batch pipeline with delete-original on.

steps.title: Order the month oldest first with bursts and singles interleaved
steps.notes: The month listing returns ascending capture order and the client builds one timeline of burst blocks and single grids, so a month reads from the 1st onwards.

steps.title: Non-blocking FIFO job queue for library actions
steps.notes: Server-side in-memory queue runs compress/trash/archive/focused-review jobs one at a time, waits for the single optimizer slot instead of failing, isolates each failure, caps history at 200 jobs, and lets a still-queued job be cancelled. Focused-review jobs apply configured tags without archiving and report per-asset outcomes. The UI polls the queue, disables assets with a pending job, and no longer blocks on a job.

steps.title: Tag compressed replacements as optimized and surface that in the month view
steps.notes: The replacement is tagged `optimized` (upserted by name) and verified with the copied tags before any deletion; the month listing marks tagged assets via SearchFilter.tagIds and tiles show an optimized badge.

steps.title: Live photo tab: unlink and trash paired motion videos
steps.notes: New tab lists stills that still reference a motion video (SearchFilter.isMotion, guarded by livePhotoVideoId) with load-more paging. Unlinking uses PUT /assets/{id} with livePhotoVideoId null and only trashes the video after Immich confirms the link is gone. An optional flag then compresses each unlinked still with bestProfileFor (AVIF per source family), grouped per profile and run through the existing batch pipeline once the videos are gone. Motion links are validated (different id, untrashed video asset) before anything is unlinked or trashed, replacements must be readable back with the exact uploaded size before an original is removed, and an interrupted compression is reported as still applying rather than failed. Selection supports click, shift-click ranges, drag-box marquee, Cmd/Ctrl+A and Esc, and photos with a queued job are excluded from every selection path.

steps.title: Publish the web image from GitHub Actions
steps.notes: Every push to web-ui builds the web target and pushes it to GHCR as <repo>-web, tagged latest and the full commit hash, with a gha layer cache and cancel-in-progress concurrency. actionlint clean; two runs on web-ui completed successfully and ghcr.io/matyifkbt/immich-upload-optimizer-web:latest resolves anonymously as a single-platform OCI manifest.

steps.title: Harden the destructive paths after a partial-failure report
steps.notes: Motion links are validated (different id, untrashed video) before unlinking or trashing, a replacement must be readable back from Immich with exactly the uploaded byte count before any original is removed, and a compression run that is still applying is reported as such instead of failed. Note the upstream release.yaml still pins action versions whose runners GitHub has removed.

steps.title: Hide queued assets from the month view immediately
steps.notes: The cleanup tab drops the assets of an archive, trash, or compression job from the grid the moment the job is queued and puts back anything the job did not settle, so the month only shows unhandled assets.

steps.title: Operator-defined tag-and-archive buttons from EXTRA_BUTTONS
steps.notes: EXTRA_BUTTONS parses comma-separated label:lucide-icon pairs at startup, exposes them through GET /api/config, and queues a tagArchive job that tags each asset with its label and only archives after Immich confirms the tag count. The server rejects any tag that no configured button declares.

steps.title: Open an asset in Immich from its thumbnail
steps.notes: Month view thumbnails link to https://my.immich.app/photos/<id>, the link helper that redirects to the user's own instance; marking stays on the Keep and Trash buttons and the desktop right click.

steps.title: Recognized faces under each asset in the month view
steps.notes: The month listing requests withPeople, keeps named visible people, and each tile shows up to four face thumbnails served through the new /api/people/{id}/thumbnail proxy, each linking to https://my.immich.app/people/<id>. Requires the person.read permission.

steps.title: Allow disabling the built-in HTTP Basic auth
steps.notes: WEB_AUTH_DISABLED=true skips the Basic-auth middleware and the password requirement so a proxy (Pocket ID behind oauth2-proxy, Authelia, forward auth) can authenticate callers. Only true/false are accepted; the flag is reported through GET /api/config and main() logs a warning that every request is unauthenticated. The UI carries no authentication notice: a deployment that authenticates callers in front of the service renders exactly like any other. Cross-origin write checks still apply.

steps.title: Exclude archived assets from the monthly review by default
steps.notes: The month listing asks Immich for every visibility except archive and locked unless GET /api/library/months/{year}/{month}?includeArchived=true says otherwise (the param is strict true/false, 400 otherwise), so archived assets no longer eat into the 3000-asset cap. Locked is named explicitly because Immich rejects a visibility filter that could still match a locked asset with 401 'Elevated permission is required' unless the session is elevated, and any explicit visibility filter suppresses the visibility != locked condition Immich adds by itself. The monthly tab carries an 'Include archived assets' switch that reloads the month; archived tiles are badged and never offered an archive action, per asset or per burst group, since they already left the timeline.

steps.title: Keep tab, monthly review, and search filters in the URL with nuqs
steps.notes: nuqs 2.10.2 with its plain-React adapter (NuqsAdapter in main.tsx; no router is needed, the adapter drives the History API directly). ?tab= names the open tab, the monthly review owns year/month/includeArchived/focus, and the compress form owns from/to/albumId. Tab, year, and month push history so the Back button walks tabs, years, and months; the archived/focused switches and the form fields replace the current entry so typing and toggling do not pile up history steps. Defaults (compress, the current year, month unset, archived off, focus off) are dropped from the URL.

steps.title: Virtualize the month grid and enlarge the desktop thumbnails
steps.notes: The month view renders through @tanstack/react-virtual 3.14 with useWindowVirtualizer: the timeline is cut into rows (a burst card, or up to N single images) and only the rows around the viewport are in the document, so a 3000-asset month keeps a handful of rows mounted instead of thousands of tiles. Row heights are measured (measureElement with data-index) and estimates only fill the gap until a row is seen. The track count is read from the grid's own width with a ResizeObserver and drives both the CSS grid and the row chunking, so the two cannot disagree; desktop stops at four columns instead of five, which makes every tile about a third larger. content-visibility was dropped from the month tiles because a skipped tile reports its intrinsic size and would poison the measurement. Verified by typecheck and a production Vite build only.

steps.title: Color the per-asset trash action red
steps.notes: The icon-only trash button under a single asset in the month view uses the destructive color for its icon, border and hover fill, so the destructive action is recognizable without reading the tooltip. The Keep/Trash pair inside a burst already used it.

steps.title: Count activity locally in stats.json and show it in a Stats tab
steps.notes: web/src/stats.ts keeps a versioned record at WEB_DATA_DIR/stats.json (0600, written atomically and coalesced every 500ms; a damaged file is moved aside as stats.json.corrupt instead of being overwritten). Replacements are reported by the optimizer at the point where an original is really removed, so reclaimed bytes are only counted when disk was actually freed; job outcomes (trashed, archived, motion videos dropped, jobs, failures) are recorded once per job by the queue, and tag-and-archive plus focused-review tag applications keep per-tag counts. GET /api/library/stats serves totals, per-month buckets, and per-tag counts, and a fourth tab (Stats) shows reclaimed space, replacements, trashed, archived, and dropped live-video counts plus a month-by-month table. Verified against the built server with the round-trip and corruption cases.

steps.title: Show an estimated storage size per month in the year grid
steps.notes: GET /api/library/months/{year}/storage returns one entry per populated month. Immich aggregates no sizes, so each month is sampled with the first page of its assets (withExif) and scaled by the month's heatmap count; a month that fits in its first page is measured exactly and paging only continues while that page held nothing from the month. Months are sampled four at a time and a year is cached for ten minutes; an unreadable month only loses its own estimate. The year grid shows the size (prefixed with ~ when it was scaled), tints each box from success through primary to destructive against the heaviest month of the year, and states that the numbers are estimates.

steps.title: Add opt-in focused monthly stack review
steps.notes: The month grid can launch a URL-addressable full-screen review. Local-minute still-photo stacks and one-item video stacks are presented side-by-side on desktop and as large snap cards on phones; left/right controls stage Keep/Trash, kept photos accept configured tag-only choices, recognized people are linked below each photo or selected grid cell, and a day overview shows review counts. Drafts and outcomes are saved per month in local storage, missing jobs are never retried automatically, and the per-stack FIFO job applies validated tags and non-forced trash with per-asset failure reporting. Scoped @tanstack/react-hotkeys bindings provide vim-style keyboard review (J/K between photos, 1-9 tag shortcuts, Space keep, D/Delete/Backspace trash, Enter apply, Z undo, S skip, Alt+S jump to the next burst stack, O overview, ? shortcut help, Esc back). An optional singles grid groups runs of single photos between burst stacks into 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, or 5x5 pages, with the preference remembered per browser. Focused-review grouping tests, web typecheck, and production build pass; Chromium with mock library data checked desktop/mobile layout, marking, queue advancement, and day overview. No live Immich writes or Docker image build were performed.

steps.title: User runs build, tests, and deployment verification
steps.notes: Web typecheck, focused-review unit tests, and production build pass; Chromium with mock library data checked the desktop/mobile flows. No Docker image build or live-Immich verification was performed; the user should test configured-tag and reversible-trash writes against their own instance.
